subject: Packaging pathway: phased upgrade, proration, and fallback options
messages:
From: Alexa Simmons <alexa.simmons@hightidehealth.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rizzo <tom.rizzo@hightidehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Packaging questions ahead of exec review

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our leadership asked for one clear recommendation for how to proceed with Redwood: should we take the Compact bundle plus the Embeddings add-on, or move straight to the Throughput tier with feature gating? They prefer a minimal-risk path that preserves latency SLAs for our triage flows but don't want to overcommit on reserved capacity.

Two specific asks for our exec meeting on Tuesday:
- A short note on proration if we upgrade mid-quarter (how do we credit unused commit vs. prorated billing?)
- A fallback plan if we hit sustained spike costs — can we automatically route to a quantized model variant or throttle non-critical routes?

I've attached our current usage snapshot (aggregated). Can you send a one-page recommendation and the pricing snapshot?

Best,
Alexa
Head of Product, Hightide Health

Attachments: usage_snapshot_jun.zip (zip)
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alexa Simmons <alexa.simmons@hightidehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging questions ahead of exec review

Alexa — thanks for the context and the snapshot. Short answer up front: for a low-risk path that preserves latency and keeps cost predictable, we usually recommend a phased upgrade to Throughput (reserve a small baseline commit) + Embeddings as an on-demand add-on, with automatic model-variant fallbacks and a routing policy for non-critical traffic.

Summary (one pager for your deck):
- Phased upgrade: start with a 3-month baseline commit at 40% of projected peak throughput, keep compact bundle features, and enable Embeddings as metered add-on. This gives reserved capacity for low-latency triage while avoiding full cost of a large commit.
- Proration: we credit unused reserved capacity on a pro-rata basis for the remainder of the billing period in token-equivalent units. Credits apply to future invoices or can be used to offset overage for 6 months. We can provide a formal proration formula for the deck (see attached spreadsheet).
- Fallbacks: implement a policy that routes to a quantized variant (compatible model family) when latency SLO is still acceptable, and a secondary policy that throttles non-essential routes (batching + queueing) when cost thresholds hit. We will include a recommended routing policy and example SLO thresholds.

I've attached: pricing_snapshot_q2.pdf and proposed-map-vs-bundle.xlsx (proposed proration math + sample invoice). Ben and Lauren are cc'ed to confirm discount/credit language we can offer in an exec-friendly slide.

Would you like a very short slide (1) and a single-sentence exec summary we can present verbally?

Thanks,
Priyom
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_snapshot_q2.pdf, proposed-map-vs-bundle.xlsx
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging pathway: phased upgrade, proration, and fallback options

Quick internal note on concessions and guardrails before we finalize the slide for Alexa:

- Discount cadence: Given Hightide's ARR profile and pilot KPIs, we can offer an initial 12% commit discount on the 3-month baseline if they sign a 9-month bridge (converts to 6% if they don't commit to a longer reserved term). Keep the discount contingent on a mutual action plan (MAP) and usage milestones.
- Proration language: accept the standard pro-rata crediting but also offer a one-time invoice credit equal to unused commit for first upgrade to build trust (to be documented in the amendment). That credit should be capped (e.g., up to 25% of first invoice) to limit exposure.
- Fallbacks & SRE: Karthik, can you draft the routing policy bullet points (quantized fallback thresholds, route-by-priority, circuit-breaker window) so we can include an operations slide?

If that sounds good I'll produce a clean exec-ready slide and a one-liner summary.

—Ben
Director, Sales Engineering
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging pathway: phased upgrade, proration, and fallback options

Ben / team — draft routing policy bullets below (for Alexa's one-pager and ops slide). I'll add examples to the MAP doc in Drive.

Routing policy - draft:
1) Latency-first routes (triage/inference): route to reserved Throughput pool. If average p95 latency > 350ms for 5 consecutive minutes, failover to quantized-compatible variant in the same family (expected latency +60-90ms, cost -35%).
2) Non-critical routes (analytics, enrichment): when cost-per-token over rolling 24h > threshold X (configurable), switch to batched mode with increased max-latency (p95 target up to 1s) and fall back to queued processing for a defined window.
3) Circuit breaker: if cost rate > 200% of baseline for 30m, throttle low-priority routes and send alert to Hightide SRE + account team. Manual override available for escalation window.
4) Grace credits: apply one-time unused-commit credit on first mid-quarter upgrade (as Ben suggested), then revert to standard pro-rata for subsequent changes.

I'll push the short bullets into the MAP doc and share the Drive link. Priyom — once you approve I'll finalize the slide and the single-sentence exec summary.

—Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
